title: Definite and Indefinite Articles Across Three Genders
subtitle: Mastering masculine, feminine, and neuter articles in the nominative case
keyPoint: Every Greek noun has a grammatical gender (masculine, feminine, or neuter) signaled by its nominative definite (ο, η, το) or indefinite (ένας, μια, ένα) article.

examples.en: Ο φίλος μου είναι εδώ.
Ένας σκύλος τρέχει γρήγορα.
Η πόρτα είναι ανοιχτή.
Θέλω μια καρέκλα, παρακαλώ.
Το νερό είναι κρύο.

mistakes.note: Although 'κορίτσι' means girl, its grammatical gender is neuter and requires 'το'.
Masculine nouns ending in -ος take the indefinite article 'ένας', not neuter 'ένα'.
The noun 'ποτό' is neuter and must take 'ένα', matching its gender.

quiz.question: Choose the correct article: '___ αδελφός μου λέγεται Πέτρος.' (My brother is named Petros.)
quiz.explanation: 'Αδελφός' is a masculine noun ending in -ος, so it takes the definite article 'ο'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct article: 'Έχω ___ ιδέα!' (I have an idea!)
quiz.explanation: 'Ιδέα' is feminine ending in -α, requiring the indefinite article 'μια'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct article: '___ σπίτι είναι όμορφο.' (The house is beautiful.)
quiz.explanation: 'Σπίτι' is a neuter noun ending in -ι, so the definite article is 'το'.

quiz.question: Choose the correct article: 'Εκεί είναι ___ ταξί.' (There is a taxi.)
quiz.explanation: 'Ταξί' is an indeclinable neuter noun and takes the indefinite article 'ένα'.

tip: Look at noun endings for handy gender clues: masculine nouns usually end in -ος, -ης, or -ας; feminine in -α or -η; and neuter in -ο, -ι, or -μα.

title: Nominative vs Accusative in Singular Nouns
subtitle: Distinguishing subjects from direct objects and knowing when to keep final -ν
keyPoint: Direct objects take the accusative case, dropping the final -ς from masculine nominative nouns and retaining final -ν on articles only before vowels and plosive consonants (κ, π, τ, ξ, ψ, μπ, ντ, γκ, τσ, τζ).

cells: τον always keeps -ν in modern standard usage
την keeps -ν before vowels and κ, π, τ, ξ, ψ, etc.
Neuters stay identical in nominative and accusative

examples.en: Ο Νίκος περιμένει τον καθηγητή.
Διαβάζω τη λέξη προσεκτικά.
Γνωρίζω την κοπέλα από το σχολείο.
Πίνω το τσάι μου κάθε πρωί.
Ένας άντρας ψάχνει έναν φίλο.

mistakes.note: Direct objects require the accusative case ('τον άντρα'), not the nominative ('ο άντρας').
The feminine article drops -ν before 'θ', because 'θ' is not a vowel or plosive stop.
Masculine nouns ending in -ος drop the final -ς when declined into accusative singular.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Έχω ___ αδελφό.' (I have a brother.)
quiz.explanation: 'Αδελφός' becomes accusative 'αδελφό', taking the masculine accusative article 'έναν'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ανοίγω ___ πόρτα.' (I open the door.)
quiz.explanation: The feminine noun 'πόρτα' starts with 'π', so the article retains its final -ν ('την').

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ψάχνει ___ καθηγητή του.' (He is looking for his teacher.)
quiz.explanation: 'Καθηγητής' is a masculine direct object in the accusative, taking the article 'τον'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Ακούω ___ φωνή σου.' (I hear your voice.)
quiz.explanation: The feminine noun 'φωνή' begins with 'φ', so the accusative article drops -ν and becomes 'τη'.

tip: Neuter singular nouns (το παιδί, το βιβλίο) never change form between nominative and accusative, making them the easiest direct objects to use!

title: Present Tense Active: Group A Verbs (-ω)
subtitle: Conjugating first-conjugation regular verbs with unstressed stems
keyPoint: Group A verbs carry stress on the stem syllable and take the standard regular active endings: -ω, -εις, -ει, -ουμε, -ετε, -ουν(ε).

examples.en: Εγώ κάνω μια σημαντική ερώτηση.
Εσύ ξέρεις την απάντηση;
Ο Πέτρος μένει κοντά στο πάρκο.
Εμείς μαθαίνουμε ελληνικά μαζί.
Τα παιδιά γράφουν στο τετράδιο.

mistakes.note: The first-person plural ending is spelled with -ουμε (-ου-), never -ομε.
Second-person singular takes -εις (-ει- with -ς), whereas -ει is for the third person singular.
First person singular 'I have' is 'έχω' with an -ω ending, not 'έχει'.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form: 'Εμείς ___ στο κέντρο.' (We live in the center.)
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural ('εμείς') takes the ending -ουμε, so 'μένουμε' is correct.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form: 'Τι ___ εσείς;' (What are you [pl.] doing?)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person plural ('εσείς') ending is -ετε: 'κάνετε'.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form: 'Η Μαρία ___ καλά αγγλικά.' (Maria knows good English.)
quiz.explanation: Maria is 3rd person singular ('αυτή'), requiring the -ει ending: 'ξέρει'.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form: 'Τα παιδιά ___ ένα ποίημα.' (The children are writing a poem.)
quiz.explanation: 'Τα παιδιά' is 3rd person plural ('αυτά'), taking -ουν(ε): 'γράφουν'.

tip: Subject pronouns (εγώ, εσύ, etc.) are usually dropped in Greek because the verb ending already specifies who is doing the action.

title: Present Tense Active: Group B Verbs (-άω/-ώ, -ώ/-είς)
subtitle: Conjugating contract verbs stressed on the final syllable
keyPoint: Group B verbs place the primary accent directly on their final present tense endings and are divided into two subgroups: B1 (-άω/-ώ, -άς, -άει) and B2 (-ώ, -είς, -εί).

examples.en: Η Ελένη μιλάει πολύ γρήγορα.
Εμείς αγαπάμε τη θάλασσα.
Δεν μπορώ να ακούσω τίποτα.
Εσείς μπορείτε να περιμένετε εδώ;
Αυτοί ζουν στην Κρήτη.

mistakes.note: Group B verbs are stressed on the ending; the first-person form is 'μιλώ' or 'μιλάω', never 'μίλω'.
'Μπορώ' belongs to Subgroup B2 (-ώ, -είς, -εί), so the 2nd person singular is 'μπορείς'.
Subgroup B1 verbs use -άμε in the 1st person plural ('μιλάμε'), not -ουμε.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form of μιλάω: 'Εσύ ___ πολύ καλά ελληνικά.' (You speak Greek very well.)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person singular form for B1 verbs (-άω) ends in -άς: 'μιλάς'.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form of μπορώ: 'Εμείς δεν ___ σήμερα.' (We cannot today.)
quiz.explanation: For subgroup B2, the 1st person plural ending is -ούμε: 'μπορούμε'.

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form of αγαπάω: 'Ο Νίκος ___ τη μουσική.' (Nikos loves music.)
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person singular for 'αγαπάω' is 'αγαπάει' (or contracted 'αγαπά').

quiz.question: Complete with the correct form of οδηγώ: 'Εσείς ___ αυτοκίνητο;' (Do you [pl.] drive a car?)
quiz.explanation: The 2nd person plural form for B2 verbs (-ώ/-είς) is -είτε: 'οδηγείτε'.

tip: When in doubt for everyday speech, B1 verbs commonly prefer the -άω forms (μιλάω, μιλάς, μιλάει, μιλάμε, μιλάτε, μιλάνε) over the older contracted variants.

title: The Irregular Verb 'Είμαι' and Existential 'Έχει'
subtitle: Conjugating 'to be' and expressing 'there is / there are' impersonally
keyPoint: 'Είμαι' expresses identity, origin, and conditions using passive-like personal endings, while the impersonal 3rd-person singular 'έχει' equates to 'there is' or 'there are'.

cells: I am / you are / he is
we are / you are / they are

examples.en: Εμείς είμαστε πολύ κουρασμένοι σήμερα.
Αυτός είναι ο καινούριος συνάδελφος.
Πού είστε τώρα;
Έχει έναν καλό φούρνο στον δρόμο.
Δεν έχει καθόλου γάλα στο ψυγείο.

mistakes.note: Do not combine 'υπάρχουν' and 'έχει'; use either verb alone, with 'έχει' being the most common everyday expression for 'there are'.
'Είσαστε' (or 'είστε') is for 2nd person plural 'εσείς'; 3rd person plural 'they are' is 'είναι'.
To say 'there is/are' existentially, 'έχει' must stay fixed in the singular 3rd person.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Εμείς ___ από την Ελλάδα.' (We are from Greece.)
quiz.explanation: 'Είμαστε' is the 1st person plural form of 'είμαι' corresponding to 'εμείς'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: '___ ένα φαρμακείο εδώ κοντά;' (Is there a pharmacy nearby?)
quiz.explanation: Impersonal 'έχει' is used for existential statements meaning 'is there / there is'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Πού ___ εσύ;' (Where are you?)
quiz.explanation: 'Είσαι' is the 2nd person singular form matching 'εσύ'.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'Στο τραπέζι ___ πολλά βιβλία.' (There are many books on the table.)
quiz.explanation: Existential 'there are' remains strictly impersonal 3rd person singular 'έχει', even with plural items.

tip: Notice that 'είναι' serves as both 'he/she/it is' AND 'they are' — the context and surrounding noun always clarify whether it is singular or plural!

title: Negation Particles: Δεν vs Μην
subtitle: Mastering real-world statements versus prohibitions and wishes
keyPoint: Use δεν to negate factual statements in the indicative mood, and use μην for negative commands, wishes, and after subjunctive markers.

cells: I want you not to be late.

useCases.label: Stating Negative Facts
useCases.example: Ο Νίκος δεν πίνει καφέ το βράδυ.

examples.en: Δεν καταλαβαίνω τι λες.
Μην τρέχεις τόσο γρήγορα!
Προτιμώ να μην πάω στο πάρτι.
Αυτός δεν θέλει να φάει κρέας.
Μη φωνάζεις, το παιδί κοιμάται.

mistakes.note: To give a negative command ('Don't speak!'), use μην/μη with the subjunctive/present, never simple indicative negation with δεν.
After the subjunctive particle να, negation always requires μην instead of δεν.
Factual knowledge is stated in the indicative mood, which strictly takes δεν.

quiz.question: I do not understand Greek very well.
quiz.explanation: A factual statement about oneself requires the indicative negation particle 'δεν'.

quiz.question: Don't open the window, please!
quiz.explanation: Negative commands and prohibitions require 'μην'.

quiz.question: Maria tries not to eat sweets.
quiz.explanation: Subjunctive clauses introduced by 'να' must be negated with 'μην'.

quiz.question: They are not coming to the cinema tonight.
quiz.explanation: Declarative present-tense statements require 'δεν'.

tip: Keep the final -ν on both 'δεν' and 'μην' when the following word starts with a vowel or the stops κ, π, τ, ξ, ψ, μπ, ντ, γκ, τσ, τζ!

title: The Genitive Case for Possession
subtitle: Expressing ownership, family relations, and descriptions across genders
keyPoint: Nouns and definite articles shift endings in the genitive case to indicate 'of' or ownership, matching gender and number.

useCases.label: Possession & Ownership
useCases.example: Το αυτοκίνητο του πατέρα είναι παλιό.

useCases.label: Origin & Specific Names
useCases.example: Το κέντρο της πόλης έχει πολλή κίνηση.

examples.en: Αυτό είναι το βιβλίο του καθηγητή.
Η τσάντα της Μαρίας είναι καινούρια.
Η πόρτα του σπιτιού είναι ανοιχτή.
Τα ονόματα των μαθητών είναι στη λίστα.
Το χρώμα του προβλήματος είναι περίπλοκο.

mistakes.note: Do not translate English 'of' with the preposition 'από'; standard Greek expresses possessive ownership directly via the genitive case.
Remember to inflect both the article and the feminine noun ending into the genitive (-ης).
Neuter nouns ending in -ι add -ού in the genitive singular (παιδί -> παιδιού).

quiz.question: This is Peter's coat (ο Πέτρος).
quiz.explanation: Masculine names ending in -ος take the genitive article 'του' and drop -ς to end in '-ου'.

quiz.question: The keys of the room (το δωμάτιο) are on the table.
quiz.explanation: Neuter nouns in -ο take the genitive article 'του' and end in '-ου' in the singular.

quiz.question: The voice of the singer (η τραγουδίστρια) is wonderful.
quiz.explanation: Feminine nouns in -α take the feminine genitive article 'της' and suffix '-ας'.

quiz.question: The parents of the children (τα παιδιά) arrived early.
quiz.explanation: Plural genitive across all genders uses the article 'των' and the ending '-ων'.

tip: All plural genitive nouns in Greek end in -ων, and the definite article for every gender in the plural genitive is always των!

title: Aorist Active: Stem Mutations
subtitle: Mastering the simple past tense and consonant mergers
keyPoint: The active Aorist combines past endings with a sigmatic suffix that merges with the stem consonant into either -ψ- or -ξ-.

useCases.label: Sequential Past Events
useCases.example: Άνοιξα την πόρτα και μπήκα μέσα.

useCases.label: Specific Moment in Time
useCases.example: Το μάθημα άρχισε στις οκτώ το πρωί.

examples.en: Χθες έγραψα όλα τα μηνύματα.
Η Ελένη άνοιξε το παράθυρο.
Τα παιδιά διάβασαν το νέο βιβλίο.
Μαγειρέψαμε ένα νόστιμο φαγητό.
Έκλεισες την πόρτα πριν φύγεις;

mistakes.note: Labial stem verbs (like γράφ-ω) merge with the past marker to form -ψ- (έγραψα).
Velar stems (like ανοίγ-ω) merge with the -σ- of the aorist into -ξ- (άνοιξα).
The past stress prefix (augment ε-) only appears when the verb needs an extra syllable to place stress on the antepenult.

quiz.question: Yesterday I cooked (μαγειρεύω) pastitsio.
quiz.explanation: Verbs in -εύω change their stem ending to -εψ- in the aorist: μαγείρεψα.

quiz.question: Who opened (ανοίγω) the store?
quiz.explanation: Velar verbs with -γ- mutate to -ξ- in the Aorist: άνοιξε.

quiz.question: We bought (αγοράζω) a new house.
quiz.explanation: Verbs ending in -ζω drop the dental consonant and simply take -σ-: αγοράσαμε.

quiz.question: They drank (πίνω -> ήπια) all the milk.
quiz.explanation: The verb πίνω has an irregular strong Aorist stem: ήπια / ήπιαν.

tip: Remember the phone formula: π, β, φ become ψ (like Greek psi), and κ, γ, χ become ξ (like Greek xi)!

title: Imperfect vs Aorist: Past Aspect
subtitle: Choosing between continuous background and punctual finished events
keyPoint: Use the Imperfect (Παρατατικός) for ongoing, habitual, or repeated past actions, and the Aorist (Αόριστος) for single, completed events.

examples.en: Κάθε καλοκαίρι πηγαίναμε στο χωριό.
Μια φορά πήγαμε στο χωριό με τρένο.
Μαγείρευα όταν κόπηκε το ρεύμα.
Ξαφνικά κόπηκε το ρεύμα.
Χθες έβρεχε όλη μέρα.

mistakes.wrong: Όταν ήμουν παιδί, πήγα κάθε μέρα στην παραλία.
mistakes.right: Όταν ήμουν παιδί, πήγαινα κάθε μέρα στην παραλία.
mistakes.note: Habitual or repeated past actions ('κάθε μέρα') require the Imperfect (πήγαινα), not the Aorist (πήγα).

mistakes.wrong: Χθες διάβαζα ένα άρθρο και το τελείωσα.
mistakes.right: Χθες διάβασα ένα άρθρο και το τελείωσα.
mistakes.note: When a past action is brought to a definite, completed finish, use the Aorist (διάβασα).

mistakes.wrong: Ενώ περπάτησα στο δρόμο, είδα ένα σκύλο.
mistakes.right: Ενώ περπατούσα στο δρόμο, είδα ένα σκύλο.
mistakes.note: Clauses introduced by ενώ ('while') set an ongoing background scene and require the Imperfect.

quiz.question: Every summer my family ___ in the sea.
quiz.explanation: The phrase 'Every summer' denotes repeated habitual action, requiring the Imperfect (κολυμπούσε).

quiz.question: Yesterday at five o'clock, the courier ___ the package.
quiz.explanation: A specific punctual completed event in the past uses the Aorist (έφερε).

quiz.question: While George ___ dinner, the phone rang.
quiz.explanation: An ongoing background action interrupted by another requires the Imperfect (ετοίμαζε).

quiz.question: Suddenly, it ___ to rain.
quiz.explanation: 'Ξαφνικά' (suddenly) marks an instantaneous entry into an event, triggering the Aorist (άρχισε).

tip: Ask yourself: Was it a movie scene unfolding over time (Imperfect), or a snapshot photo of a finished action (Aorist)?

title: Weak Personal Clitic Pronoun Placement
subtitle: Placing direct and indirect unstressed pronouns accurately
keyPoint: Weak object pronouns precede finite conjugated verbs, but attach directly to the end of affirmative imperative forms.

examples.en: Τον ξέρω πολλά χρόνια.
Δώσε μου το μολύβι σου.
Μην της μιλάς τώρα, είναι θυμωμένη.
Σας παρακαλώ, βοηθήστε μας.
Θέλω να σου πω κάτι.

mistakes.note: In indicative statements, weak clitic pronouns must stand directly before the conjugated verb.
In positive imperative commands, the clitic pronoun always follows the verb.
Negative commands place the clitic before the verb and immediately after the negative particle μη(ν).

quiz.question: I see her (αυτήν -> τη / την) every afternoon.
quiz.explanation: In indicative statements, clitics go before the conjugated verb: Τη βλέπω.

quiz.question: Give me (μου) the ticket!
quiz.explanation: Affirmative imperative verbs place the weak clitic pronoun directly after the verb: Δώσε μου.

quiz.question: Do not tell him (του) anything!
quiz.explanation: In negative commands, the clitic is placed between 'μην' and the verb: Μην του πεις.

quiz.question: When both clitics appear together, indirect precedes direct: He gave it to me.
quiz.explanation: In pre-verbal position, the indirect pronoun (μου) precedes the direct accusative pronoun (το): Μου το έδωσε.

tip: If a positive imperative verb is stressed on the third syllable from the end (antepenult), adding a clitic forces an extra accent on the last syllable: π.χ., διάβασέ το!

title: Future Tenses with 'Θα': Continuous vs Simple Dependent
subtitle: Master the distinction between ongoing and one-time future actions
keyPoint: Use 'θα' with the present stem for continuous or repeated future actions, but use 'θα' with the dependent (aorist) stem for single, completed events.

useCases.label: Single Event (Simple)
useCases.example: Αύριο θα πάρω το τρένο στις οκτώ.

useCases.label: Ongoing Process (Continuous)
useCases.example: Όλο το απόγευμα θα διαβάζω στη βιβλιοθήκη.

useCases.label: Habitual Future (Continuous)
useCases.example: Από τον άλλο μήνα θα πηγαίνω στο γυμναστήριο κάθε μέρα.

examples.en: Απόψε θα μαγειρέψω ένα ωραίο φαγητό.
Κάθε πρωί θα πίνω καφέ στο μπαλκόνι.
Αύριο στις πέντε θα ταξιδεύουμε για την Κρήτη.
Μόλις φτάσω στο σπίτι, θα σε πάρω τηλέφωνο.
Τον επόμενο χειμώνα θα μαθαίνω ισπανικά κάθε Τρίτη.

mistakes.wrong: Αύριο θα γράφω ένα γράμμα στη μαμά μου.
mistakes.right: Αύριο θα γράψω ένα γράμμα στη μαμά μου.
mistakes.note: Writing one letter tomorrow is a single, complete action, so you must use the simple future stem (γράψ-), not the continuous (γράφ-).

mistakes.wrong: Κάθε μέρα θα διαβάσω για δύο ώρες.
mistakes.right: Κάθε μέρα θα διαβάζω για δύο ώρες.
mistakes.note: Repeated daily habits require the continuous stem (διαβάζ-), not the one-time simple stem (διαβάσ-).

mistakes.wrong: Θα πάω κάθε Κυριακή στη γιαγιά.
mistakes.right: Θα πηγαίνω κάθε Κυριακή στη γιαγιά.
mistakes.note: Recurring habitual actions ('κάθε Κυριακή') demand the continuous verb form 'θα πηγαίνω'.

quiz.question: Tomorrow I will buy a new car. (one-time event)
quiz.explanation: A single future event requires 'θα' followed by the simple dependent stem (-ασ-).

quiz.question: Next year I will be studying every afternoon.
quiz.explanation: Habitual, repeated future actions need the continuous future with the present stem.

quiz.question: Tonight we will watch the new film. (single event)
quiz.explanation: Watching a film once tonight calls for the simple dependent form of 'βλέπω', which is 'θα δούμε'.

quiz.question: All night long the wind will be blowing.
quiz.explanation: Actions that extend continuously over a period ('όλη τη νύχτα') take the continuous future.

tip: Time markers are your best clue: words like 'αύριο', 'απόψε', and 'μόλις' usually take simple future (θα γράψω), whereas 'κάθε μέρα' and 'όλη μέρα' take continuous future (θα γράφω).

title: Active Imperative: Continuous vs Punctual Commands
subtitle: Give direct orders, advice, and instructions with the correct aspect
keyPoint: Use the punctual imperative for one-time instructions and the continuous imperative for ongoing habits, while always using 'μη(ν)' + subjunctive for negative commands.

examples.en: Άνοιξε το παράθυρο, κάνει ζέστη.
Διάβαζε καθημερινά για να μάθεις γρήγορα.
Περιμένετε εδώ για λίγα λεπτά.
Μην αγγίζεις τα εκθέματα στο μουσείο.
Πες μου όλη την αλήθεια τώρα.

mistakes.note: Greek has no direct negative imperative; use 'μη(ν)' plus the dependent subjunctive (-εις), never the positive imperative form.

mistakes.wrong: Κάθε πρωί πιες ένα ποτήρι γάλα.
mistakes.right: Κάθε πρωί πίνε ένα ποτήρι γάλα.
mistakes.note: General habitual instructions over time require the continuous imperative (πίνε), not the punctual (πιες).
Ongoing actions while someone speaks require continuous aspect (άκουγε).

quiz.question: Turn off the light right now! (to one person, punctual)
quiz.explanation: For a single, immediate command to 'εσύ', use the punctual imperative 'κλείσε'.

quiz.question: Don't eat the cake! (one-time prohibition to 'εσύ')
quiz.explanation: Negative punctual commands use 'μη' + simple subjunctive: 'μη φας'.

quiz.question: Practice Greek every single day! (habitual advice to 'εσύ')
quiz.explanation: 'Μίλαγε' (or 'μίλα') is the continuous imperative expressing a repeated long-term habit.

quiz.question: Tell me your name! (polite/plural form)
quiz.explanation: 'Πείτε' is the punctual imperative plural form of the irregular verb 'λέω'.

tip: Never put 'μη' directly before an imperative word like 'γράψε'—always switch to the subjunctive: 'μη γράψεις'!

title: Mediopassive Voice Present Tense (-ομαι, -ιέμαι)
subtitle: Conjugate reflexive, reciprocal, and passive actions in the present
keyPoint: Greek mediopassive verbs end in -ομαι (Group A) or -ιέμαι/-ούμαι (Group B) and describe passive, reflexive, or state-change actions.

cells: I wash myself / I am loved
you wash yourself / you are loved

useCases.label: Reflexive Action
useCases.example: Ο Νίκος ντύνεται γρήγορα κάθε πρωί.

useCases.label: True Passive
useCases.example: Τα ελληνικά βιβλία διαβάζονται σε όλο τον κόσμο.

examples.en: Το μουσείο κλείνεται νωρίς κάθε Κυριακή.
Εμείς σκεφτόμαστε σοβαρά να αλλάξουμε δουλειά.
Πώς γράφεται αυτή η λέξη;
Τα παιδιά κουράζονται εύκολα στο σχολείο.
Η Μαρία και ο Γιώργος αγαπιούνται πάρα πολύ.

mistakes.wrong: Το φαγητό μαγειρεύει από τη μητέρα.
mistakes.right: Το φαγητό μαγειρεύεται από τη μητέρα.
mistakes.note: Active 'μαγειρεύει' means 'cooks'; the food is cooked, so passive 'μαγειρεύεται' is required.
'Πλένω' needs an object (I wash the car). To wash yourself, use mediopassive 'πλένομαι'.
The mediopassive form already carries reflexive/reciprocal meaning; do not add redundant object pronouns.

quiz.question: How is this word pronounced? ('This word ___')
quiz.explanation: The subject 'η λέξη' is 3rd person singular, needing 'προφέρεται' (is pronounced).

quiz.question: We see each other every weekend.
quiz.explanation: Reciprocal 1st person plural ('we see each other') uses the ending -όμαστε: 'βλεπόμαστε'.

quiz.question: The boy gets dressed on his own.
quiz.explanation: 3rd person singular mediopassive for 'he gets dressed' is 'ντύνεται'.

quiz.question: Many languages are spoken in Europe.
quiz.explanation: The plural subject 'πολλές γλώσσες' requires the 3rd person plural passive 'μιλιούνται'.

tip: Deponent verbs in Greek (like έρχομαι, θυμάμαι, κοιμάμαι) use passive endings but always have active meanings in English.

title: Subjunctive Mood with 'Να' (Aspectual Choice)
subtitle: Express wants, intentions, and necessity while choosing aspect
keyPoint: Follow the particle 'να' with the continuous stem for ongoing desires or habits, and with the simple dependent stem for single, specific goals.

cells: I want to dance (this one dance)

useCases.label: Desire for One Event
useCases.example: Θέλω να πιω έναν κρύο καφέ.

useCases.label: Necessity / Obligation
useCases.example: Πρέπει να πληρώσουμε τον λογαριασμό σήμερα.

useCases.label: Ongoing Preference
useCases.example: Μου αρέσει να ξυπνάω νωρίς το πρωί.

examples.en: Μπορείς να μου δώσεις το αλάτι;
Πρέπει να τρως φρούτα κάθε μέρα.
Ελπίζω να βρεις τα κλειδιά σου σύντομα.
Δεν θέλω να περιμένω στην ουρά με τις ώρες.
Αποφάσισα να αγοράσω ένα καινούριο διαμέρισμα.

mistakes.wrong: Θέλω να πίνω έναν καφέ τώρα.
mistakes.right: Θέλω να πιω έναν καφέ τώρα.
mistakes.note: Drinking one specific coffee right now is a punctual, completed action; use 'να πιω', not 'να πίνω'.

mistakes.wrong: Μου αρέσει να διαβάσω κάθε βράδυ.
mistakes.right: Μου αρέσει να διαβάζω κάθε βράδυ.
mistakes.note: Liking a recurring activity ('κάθε βράδυ') demands the continuous subjunctive 'να διαβάζω'.

mistakes.wrong: Πρέπει να πηγαίνω αμέσως στον γιατρό.
mistakes.right: Πρέπει να πάω αμέσως στον γιατρό.
mistakes.note: Going immediately right now is a single event, requiring simple subjunctive 'να πάω'.

quiz.question: I would like to order right now. (single action)
quiz.explanation: A single, specific order requires the dependent simple stem: 'να παραγγείλω'.

quiz.question: You should exercise every single day. (habitual)
quiz.explanation: Daily ongoing habits take the continuous subjunctive: 'να γυμνάζεσαι'.

quiz.question: Can you open the door, please? (single event)
quiz.explanation: Opening the door once in this moment calls for the simple stem 'να ανοίξεις'.

quiz.question: We plan to live in Athens permanently.
quiz.explanation: Living permanently represents an ongoing state, fitting the continuous subjunctive 'να μένουμε'.

tip: Whenever English uses 'to + infinitive' (e.g., 'I want to go'), Greek nearly always replaces it with 'να' + subjunctive.

title: Passive Aorist (Simple Past Passive in -θηκα)
subtitle: Form and use completed past passive actions ending in -θηκα
keyPoint: The simple past of mediopassive verbs is formed with the suffix -θηκα, -θηκες, -θηκε and active past personal endings.

useCases.label: Completed Passive Event
useCases.example: Το σπίτι πουλήθηκε την περασμένη εβδομάδα.

examples.en: Η συναυλία ακυρώθηκε λόγω βροχής.
Χθες το βράδυ κουράστηκα πάρα πολύ στη δουλειά.
Γεννήθηκα στην Αθήνα πριν από είκοσι χρόνια.
Όλα τα εισιτήρια πληρώθηκαν με κάρτα.
Σηκωθήκαμε νωρίς για να προλάβουμε την πτήση.

mistakes.wrong: Το γράμμα έγραψε από τον Πέτρο.
mistakes.right: Το γράμμα γράφτηκε από τον Πέτρο.
mistakes.note: 'Έγραψε' is active ('he wrote'). The letter was written, so use the passive past 'γράφτηκε'.
'Κοιμάμαι' is a deponent verb; its past tense requires the mediopassive ending -ήθηκα ('κοιμηθήκαμε').
If you paid Maria, use the active 'πλήρωσα'. 'Πληρώθηκα' means 'I received my salary / I was paid'.

quiz.question: Yesterday the shop was closed early.
quiz.explanation: The passive simple past for 'was closed' is 'κλείστηκε' (from κλείνομαι).

quiz.question: We met each other last summer in Crete.
quiz.explanation: 1st person plural past passive for reciprocal 'we met' is 'γνωριστήκαμε'.

quiz.question: Where were you born? (to singular 'εσύ')
quiz.explanation: 'Γεννήθηκες' is the 2nd person singular past passive of 'γεννιέμαι' (to be born).

quiz.question: They woke up late on Sunday.
quiz.explanation: 3rd person plural past passive of 'σηκώνομαι' (to get up) is 'σηκώθηκαν'.

tip: Notice that even though the stem is passive (-θηκ-), the personal endings (-α, -ες, -ε, -αμε, -ατε, -αν) are identical to the active simple past!

title: Clitic Doubling and Flexible Word Order
subtitle: Highlighting topics and emphasis using weak object pronouns
keyPoint: Clitic doubling pairs a weak object pronoun with a full noun phrase to mark information as an established topic or to bring it into focus.

useCases.label: Topic Topicalization
useCases.example: Αυτό το τραγούδι το ξέρω πολύ καλά.

examples.en: Τον είδα τον Γιώργο στην πλατεία.
Το αυτοκίνητο το πούλησε πριν από έναν μήνα.
Της μίλησα της Ελένης για το πρόγραμμα.
Αυτά τα νέα τα μάθαμε πολύ νωρίς.
Δεν την ξέρω αυτή την κοπέλα.

mistakes.note: Indefinite or non-specific direct objects cannot normally undergo clitic doubling.
In indicative sentences, weak object clitics must precede the finite verb, not follow it.
Make sure the clitic pronoun matches the case of the full noun phrase (accusative τον for direct objects).

quiz.question: Choose the natural way to say 'As for that letter, I sent it': 'Εκείνο το γράμμα ___.'
quiz.explanation: When the direct object is topicalized at the beginning, Greek requires the matching accusative clitic pronoun (το) before the verb.

quiz.question: Complete the doubled question: '___ είδες τη Μαρία στο γραφείο;'
quiz.explanation: The noun phrase 'τη Μαρία' is feminine singular accusative, so the agreeing direct clitic is 'την'.

quiz.question: Identify the incorrect usage of clitic doubling:
quiz.explanation: Indefinite noun phrases like 'μια εφημερίδα' cannot take a clitic double.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly doubles an indirect object?
options: Τον έδωσα το κλειδί του Πέτρου.
Του έδωσα το κλειδί τον Πέτρο.
Το έδωσα του Πέτρου το κλειδί.
Του έδωσα του Πέτρου το κλειδί.
quiz.explanation: The recipient 'του Πέτρου' is genitive, so it must be doubled by the matching masculine genitive clitic 'του'.

tip: Only double definite or referential noun phrases. Using a clitic with an indefinite noun like 'ένα μήλο' is grammatically incorrect in Greek.

title: Gerund (-οντας/-ώντας) vs Passive Participle (-μένος)
subtitle: Contrasting invariant adverbial actions with inflected passive states
keyPoint: Active participles ending in -οντας/-ώντας are invariable adverbs describing simultaneous actions, while passive participles ending in -μένος decline like regular adjectives.

useCases.label: Subject Modification
useCases.example: Περπατώντας στο δάσος, είδε ένα ελάφι.

examples.en: Διαβάζοντας το βιβλίο, αποκοιμήθηκε στον καναπέ.
Ήπιαμε καφέ κοιτάζοντας τη θάλασσα.
Όλα τα φώτα στο κτίριο είναι σβησμένα.
Μου έδωσε μια σπασμένη κούπα.
Γελώντας δυνατά, μπήκαν μέσα στην τάξη.

mistakes.note: The active participle in modern Greek never inflects for plural; it stays -οντας/-ώντας regardless of subject.
To describe a state or completed quality, use the inflected passive participle (-μένος), not the gerund.
Passive participles in -μένος must agree in gender, number, and case with the noun they modify.

quiz.question: Select the correct form: 'Μπήκε στο δωμάτιο ___ ένα τραγούδι.' (singing)
quiz.explanation: 'Τραγουδώντας' is the active adverbial gerund indicating an action happening concurrently with entering.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence with the correct passive participle: 'Τα παράθυρα είναι ___.' (open)
quiz.explanation: The passive participle/adjective must agree with the neuter plural noun 'τα παράθυρα' (ανοιχτά / ανοιγμένα).

quiz.question: Which word correctly completes: 'Η Μαρία έφτασε στη δουλειά εντελώς ___.' (tired)
quiz.explanation: The subject 'Η Μαρία' is feminine singular nominative, requiring 'κουρασμένη'.

quiz.question: Spell the gerund of 'κοιτάζω' (I look):
quiz.explanation: First-conjugation verbs like κοιτάζω form the gerund in -οντας (unaccented omega: κοιτάζοντας).

tip: Spelling check: verbs stressed on the stem end in -οντας (τρέχω -> τρέχοντας), while verbs stressed on the last syllable end in -ώντας (αγαπώ -> αγαπώντας).

title: Hypothetical and Counterfactual Conditionals
subtitle: Constructing potential and unreal present and past conditions
keyPoint: Counterfactual and hypothetical conditionals use 'αν' with the imperfect for present unreal scenarios and 'θα' + imperfect or pluperfect for past counterfactual outcomes.

useCases.label: Present Unreal
useCases.example: Αν είχα χρήματα, θα αγόραζα εκείνο το σπίτι.

useCases.label: Past Unreal (Counterfactual)
useCases.example: Αν είχες έρθει στην ώρα σου, θα είχαμε προλάβει το τρένο.

useCases.label: Polite Hypothesis / Wish
useCases.example: Αν ήμουν στη θέση σου, δεν θα μιλούσα.

examples.en: Αν ήξερα την απάντηση, θα σου την έλεγα.
Αν είχαμε φύγει νωρίτερα, δεν θα χάναμε την πτήση.
Αν είχα διαβάσει περισσότερο, θα είχα περάσει το μάθημα.
Τι θα έκανες αν κέρδιζες το λαχείο;
Αν δεν έβρεχε χθες, θα πηγαίναμε εκδρομή.

mistakes.wrong: Αν θα είχα χρόνο, θα ερχόμουν.
mistakes.note: Never place the particle 'θα' directly inside the 'αν' condition clause.

mistakes.wrong: Αν είχα λεφτά, θα αγοράσω αυτοκίνητο.
mistakes.right: Αν είχα λεφτά, θα αγόραζα αυτοκίνητο.
mistakes.note: Do not mix an unreal imperfect in the 'αν' clause with a simple future in the apodosis.
Present hypothetical conditionals require 'θα' + Imperfect in the main clause.

quiz.question: Choose the correct verb for a present unreal condition: 'Αν ___ πλούσιος, θα ταξίδευα παντού.'
quiz.explanation: The 'αν' clause of an unreal present condition takes the imperfect without 'θα' (ήμουν).

quiz.question: Complete the past counterfactual: 'Αν με είχες προειδοποιήσει, ___ πιο προσεκτικός.'
quiz.explanation: The apodosis (consequence) of a counterfactual condition requires 'θα' + imperfect/pluperfect (θα ήμουν / θα είχα υπάρξει).

quiz.question: Which sentence represents an impossible past counterfactual?
options: Αν είχαμε κλειδιά, θα μπαίναμε τώρα.
Αν είχες διαβάσει, θα είχες γράψει καλά.
quiz.explanation: 'Αν είχες διαβάσει, θα είχες γράψει καλά' uses the pluperfect to indicate an event that did not happen in the past.

quiz.question: Find the grammatically sound counterfactual clause:
quiz.explanation: 'Αν ερχόσουν, θα περνούσαμε υπέροχα' matches imperfect in the condition with 'θα' + imperfect in the result.

tip: Remember the Golden Rule of Greek conditionals: 'θα' belongs in the consequence clause, never inside the clause introduced by 'αν'.

title: Learned and Third-Declension Nominal Declensions
subtitle: Navigating formal nominal patterns inherited from Katharevousa
keyPoint: Fossilized third-declension learned nouns preserve archaic genitive and plural endings, such as -εως for feminine abstracts in -ση/-ξη/-ψη and -ους for neuters in -ος.

useCases.label: Formal Administrative Speech
useCases.example: Ο Υπουργός Εξωτερικών ανακοίνωσε νέα μέτρα.

useCases.label: Learned Genitives
useCases.example: Το θέμα της εκπαιδεύσεως απασχολεί τη χώρα.

examples.en: Η εξέλιξη της καταστάσεως είναι απρόβλεπτη.
Όλα τα μέλη του διοικητικού συμβουλίου συμφώνησαν.
Έγινε αναφορά στις παραμέτρους του προβλήματος.
Πρόκειται για άτομο με ιδιαίτερες πνευματικές ικανότητες.
Η τιμή του εισιτηρίου εξαρτάται από το βάθος της διαδρομής.

mistakes.note: Neuter nouns ending in -ος (το λάθος) form their plural in -η (τα λάθη), never -α.

mistakes.right: Της κυβέρνησης / Της κυβερνήσεως η απόφαση.
mistakes.note: Both forms exist, but in elevated speech -εως is favored; avoid mixing colloquial and formal stems erroneously.
Neuters in -ος take -ους in the genitive singular (το κράτος -> του κράτους).

quiz.question: Choose the genitive singular of 'η εξέλιξη' in formal Greek: 'Τα αίτια της ___.'
quiz.explanation: In formal or learned registers, feminine nouns in -ξη form their genitive in -εως (της εξελίξεως).

quiz.question: What is the nominative plural of 'το μέρος' (the part/place)?
quiz.explanation: Neuter learned nouns ending in -ος take the nominative/accusative plural ending -η (τα μέρη).

quiz.question: Complete the genitive phrase: 'Λόγω του ___ (το γεγονός).'
quiz.explanation: Third-declension neuters ending in -ός form their genitive singular with -ότος (του γεγονότος).

quiz.question: Identify the genitive singular of 'το έδαφος':
quiz.explanation: Neuters in -ος take -ους in the genitive singular: του εδάφους.

tip: Neuter nouns ending in -ος like 'το λάθος' or 'το κράτος' always form the genitive singular in -ους and the plural in -η. Never treat them like masculine -ος nouns!

title: Complement Clauses: 'Ότι' vs 'Πως' vs 'Που'
subtitle: Navigating nuanced complementizer selection across reporting and emotion
keyPoint: 'Ότι' introduces neutral factual assertions, 'πως' conveys subjective or informal reporting, and 'που' is used when the proposition is an acknowledged fact triggering an emotional reaction.

cells: Verbs of emotion, memory, sensory proof

useCases.label: Factual Declaration (Ότι)
useCases.example: Οι ειδήσεις ανέφεραν ότι ο καιρός θα χαλάσει.

useCases.label: Emotional Complement (Που)
useCases.example: Λυπάμαι που δεν μπόρεσα να σε βοηθήσω.

useCases.label: Colloquial Belief (Πως)
useCases.example: Μου φαίνεται πως δεν έχει καταλάβει τίποτα.

examples.en: Ξέρω ότι είσαι πολύ απασχολημένος.
Άκουσα πως αλλάζεις δουλειά σύντομα.
Χάρηκα πολύ που σε γνώρισα από κοντά.
Θυμάμαι που πηγαίναμε στην παραλία κάθε καλοκαίρι.
Μας διαβεβαίωσε ότι όλα ήταν εντάξει.

mistakes.note: Verbs expressing emotion (χαίρομαι, λυπάμαι, φοβάμαι) require 'που', not 'ότι'.
Verbs of wanting and requesting govern the subjunctive particle 'να', never declarative 'ότι'.

mistakes.wrong: Θυμάμαι ότι έπαιξες όταν ήσουν παιδί.
mistakes.right: Θυμάμαι που έπαιζες όταν ήσουν παιδί.
mistakes.note: When evoking vivid personal memories as lived experiences, 'που' with the imperfect is the natural choice.

quiz.question: Complete the emotional statement: 'Λυπάμαι πολύ ___ έχασες την πτήση σου.'
quiz.explanation: Verbs of emotional reaction like 'λυπάμαι' trigger the complementizer 'που'.

quiz.question: Fill in the formal declarative clause: 'Η ανακοίνωση έλεγε ___ το κατάστημα θα μείνει κλειστό.'
quiz.explanation: Formal neutral statements and official reports use 'ότι'.

quiz.question: Select the correct particle after a verb of volition: 'Ελπίζω ___ πάνε όλα καλά.'
quiz.explanation: Verbs expressing hope or anticipation frequently take 'να' to introduce subjunctive modal clauses.

quiz.question: Which verb correctly governs 'που' as a complementizer?
quiz.explanation: 'Στενοχωριέμαι' (I feel sad/upset) is an affective verb and takes 'που' (e.g., Στενοχωριέμαι που φεύγεις).

tip: Quick rule of thumb: If you can replace the connector with 'the fact that' after an emotion or memory, use 'που'. For straightforward factual reporting ('he said that'), use 'ότι'.
